chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Bukayr and Jamīl, from ʿAmr ibn Muṣʿab, who said:

I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “Do you think that the bequeather from among us bequeaths to whomever he wishes? No, by Allah! Rather, it is a covenant from the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) to one man, then another man, until it ended with himself.”

key_terms.الْمُوصِيَ: the one who appoints a successor or makes a bequest
key_terms.رَجُلٍ فَرَجُلٍ: from one man to another in succession
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah, source of the transmitted covenant
key_terms.عَهْدٌ: a binding covenant or entrusted designation
key_terms.نَفْسِهِ: himself; indicating the covenant reached the speaking Imam

ai.seo_question: Is the Imamate chosen by personal decision or by covenant from the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Imamate is not assigned by personal preference or individual choice. Rather, it is a divinely guided covenant transmitted in succession from the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) to each designated Imam.
